title: Canada 10-Year Yield Nears Three-Year High
body: Canada's 10-year government bond yield climbed to about 3.95% in September, approaching a three-year high as concerns over energy-driven inflation persisted. Oil prices advanced following a five-week pause in the rally that began after the US–Iran war, amid uncertainty surrounding diplomatic efforts to end the conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Robust US economic data reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve could deliver another interest rate hike this year. Yields on US Treasuries surged to multi-decade highs, adding pressure on Canadian bonds, whose yields typically move in line with US rates. Fed projections indicated that most policymakers anticipate one more rate increase before the end of 2026. At its September meeting, the Bank of Canada left its benchmark policy rate unchanged at 2.25%, in line with market expectations. However, it warned that inflation risks had risen and that newly imposed tariffs had increased uncertainty around the growth outlook. Governor Macklem emphasized that policymakers stand ready to raise rates further if inflation remains elevated. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Ibovespa Falls on Political and Inflation Concerns
body: The Ibovespa dropped 0.9% on Wednesday, closing at 185,814 points, pressured by new election polls and a rebound in oil prices. An AtlasIntel survey for October's presidential race showed President Lula regaining a numerical lead over Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in a simulated second-round runoff, although the two remain technically tied within the margin of error. At the same time, oil prices rose amid uncertainty surrounding diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, reinforcing concerns about energy-driven inflation. Adding to the cautious mood, the Copom minutes released yesterday were interpreted as more hawkish than markets had anticipated. Sector performance was broadly negative. Financials dragged the index lower: Itaú fell 1.9%, Bradesco and Banco do Brasil each lost 2.2%, and Itaúsa declined 1.9%. Utilities also retreated, with Sabesp down nearly 2.8%. Vale slid 1.8%, weighed down by weak profitability among Chinese steelmakers. In contrast, Petrobras advanced 2.6%, supported by higher oil prices. title: TSX Slides as Yields Hit Multi-Year Highs
body: The S&P/TSX Composite Index fell 1.6% to close at 35,751 on Wednesday as bond yields climbed to multi-year highs. Yields surged on renewed, energy-driven inflation concerns, with oil prices advancing amid uncertainty over diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Robust US economic data also reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve may deliver another rate hike this year. US Treasury yields rose to multi-decade highs, adding pressure on Canadian bonds, whose yields typically track US rates. Financials were broadly weaker, with major banks posting notable losses: RBC slipped 2%, TD Bank dropped 2.4%, BMO declined 2%, and Scotiabank fell 1.6%. Meanwhile, continued declines in gold, silver, and copper weighed on the mining sector; Agnico Eagle lost 3.9%, Barrick retreated 3.2%, and WPM sank 5.4%. title: Argentina Retail Sales Growth Accelerates
body: Argentina's retail sales climbed 23% year-on-year to ARS 707.8 billion in July 2026, quickening from a 13.4% increase in June. The strongest growth was recorded in furniture, home décor, and household textiles, up 51.7%, followed by sportswear and accessories (46.3%), entertainment and leisure (45.1%), food courts, food outlets, and kiosks (29.3%), and bookstores and stationery (24.3%). By region, sales rose 26% in Buenos Aires and 23.9% across the 24 districts of Greater Buenos Aires. In the Pampean Region, sales increased 17.6%, while the Cuyo Region posted a 17% gain. Sales in the Northern and Patagonia regions advanced 22.9% and 30.8%, respectively. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: US Stocks Fall as Yields Hit Multi-Decade Highs
body: US equity markets finished lower on Wednesday as robust economic data, a weak Treasury auction, and renewed energy-driven inflation worries pushed government bond yields to their highest levels in decades. The S&P 500 declined 0.7%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 351 points, and the Nasdaq 100 slipped 0.8% from its record high. A fresh surge in oil prices helped drive yields higher, intensifying inflation concerns. The move in yields accelerated after S&P Global PMI figures pointed to strong new orders and the fastest increases in input and output prices in several years, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve could deliver another rate hike this year. The bond selloff deepened when a five-year Treasury auction drew unexpectedly soft demand. Credit-sensitive AI hyperscalers—currently engaged in record levels of debt issuance—traded mostly lower, with Alphabet down 3.8%, Oracle off 3.1%, and Amazon falling 2.2%. Major banks also declined. Semiconductor stocks retreated as investors locked in gains from this week's rally: Nvidia slipped 1.5%, Broadcom dropped 2.6%, and Micron lost 2.2%. title: US Heating Oil Falls on Diesel Export Ban
body: US heating oil prices have retreated to about $4.80 per gallon, down from last week's record high of more than $5.20, following reports that the Trump administration is drafting a proposal to suspend diesel exports for 90 days. The plan, aimed at easing domestic energy costs, has exposed divisions within both the administration and the oil industry. In parallel, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has urged President Trump to convene a trilateral summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin, stressing that the leaders must act "as quickly as possible" to end the war. Zelenskyy also noted that he and Trump discussed an "energy ceasefire." Trump, for his part, said that Moscow has "unfortunately lost control" of its diesel sector as a result of the conflict and has previously pressed Zelenskyy to halt drone strikes on Russian oil refineries. At the same time, the partial restoration of Saudi Arabia's East–West pipeline is easing some supply concerns, even as uncertainty over the outlook for peace in the Middle East continues to cloud the market. title: Argentina's Retail Sales Growth Accelerates to 25.8% YoY in July 2026
body: Argentina's retail sector continued its strong upward trajectory in mid-2026, with July retail sales rising 25.8% year-over-year, according to the latest data updated on 23 September 2026. The figure marks a notable acceleration from June 2026, when retail sales had already posted a robust 23.7% increase compared with the same month a year earlier. The data, measured on a year-over-year basis, indicates that consumer activity strengthened further in July, as the pace of annual growth in sales outstripped that of the previous month. In this methodology, the current reading compares July 2026 retail sales to July 2025, while the previous figure compares June 2026 sales to June 2025. The back-to-back double-digit gains, and the pickup from June to July, underscore resilient demand in Argentina's consumer market, with July's performance reinforcing a trend of solid annual expansion in retail activity. title: Oil Extends Gains Amid Geopolitical Uncertainty
body: Crude oil climbed above $92.50 a barrel on Wednesday, snapping a five-session losing streak, as uncertainty lingered over the trajectory of US–Iran negotiations. At the UN General Assembly, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Tehran remained open to diplomacy but would not negotiate "under pressure." Meanwhile, Iran's military warned it was prepared to launch "more crushing" strikes in response to US President Donald Trump's earlier UN address, in which he threatened to "annihilate" Iran. Following his remarks, Trump described subsequent talks with Iranian envoys as "productive." Tehran, for its part, has signaled it could reopen the strait if Washington eases its military posture and lifts restrictions on Iranian ports. On the supply side, Saudi Arabia's partial restoration of its East–West pipeline has helped alleviate some market concerns. In a separate diplomatic development, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy urged Trump to convene a trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Zelenskyy also said that he and Trump discussed the possibility of an "energy ceasefire." The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com
